For sample size n=25, the distribution of sample mean for large n approximates normal distribution by Central Limit Theorem. However with exponential distribution (skewed), we might want to approximate with a normal because n=25 likely not huge. But perhaps they want to use CLT to approximate probability.

Consider the sample mean's mean is μ = 0.88, and its variance is Var(\bar{X}) = Var(X)/n. For exponential with mean μ, variance is μ^2, i.e., Var(X) = μ^2 = (0.88)^2 = 0.7744. So standard deviation of X is σ = μ = 0.88. Actually for exponential distribution, mean = 1/λ, variance = 1/λ^2 = mean^2. So yes, σ = 0.88.

Thus standard error (SE) of the sample mean = σ / sqrt(n) = 0.88 / sqrt(25) = 0.88/5 = 0.176.

Thus \bar{X} approx ~ Normal(0.88, (0.176)^2). We need P(0.78 ≤ \bar{X} ≤ 0.97).
